item.title: Benchmark Saturation Highlights LLMs Generating SVGs of an Armadillo on Mars
item.description:
Benchmark Saturation Highlights LLMs Generating SVGs of an Armadillo on Mars

On 6 October 2026, the community observed that a leading benchmark had become saturated, leading researchers to test frontier models with a whimsical prompt: an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars.

🔍 Overview

  • The benchmark is saturated. (Quoted by wren6991)
  • Frontier models are being evaluated using the prompt “Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars.”

🧩 Models Tested

Model Prompt Command
claude‑opus‑5.5 llm -m claude-opus-5.5 'Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars'
gpt‑6.1‑sol llm -m gpt-6.1-sol 'Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars'
gemini‑3.8‑flash llm -m gemini-3.8-flash 'Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars'
mistral‑large‑4 llm -m mistral/mistral-large-4 'Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars'

⚙️ Prompt and Output

  • The same natural‑language prompt was issued to each model.
  • Each model returned an SVG representation of the requested scene.
  • Default reasoning levels for each model are documented at: https://tools.simonwillison.net/markdown-svg-renderer?url=ht…

📊 Benchmark Note

  • The observation “The benchmark is saturated.” signals that current evaluation metrics no longer differentiate model performance, prompting creative stress tests like the armadillo SVG task.

📚 Related Context

  • Recent discussions (3 Oct 2026) highlight the need for default hard budget caps on AI resources.
  • OpenAI DevDay 2026 (29 Sep 2026) and the “2026 in LLMs (so far)” recap (27 Sep 2026) are among the recent articles surrounding these developments.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra Generates Higher‑Quality Pelican SVGs Than GPT‑5.6 Models
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra Generates Higher‑Quality Pelican SVGs Than GPT‑5.6 Models

I received access to GPT‑6 Astra and used it to generate SVG images of pelicans riding bicycles at several reasoning levels, then compared the results side‑by‑side with GPT‑5.6 models (Sol, Terra, Luna).

🔍 Overview

  • The Pelican comparison grid for Astra was created.
  • The grid includes GPT‑6 Astra images at low, medium, high, xhigh, and max reasoning levels (Astra doesn’t support reasoning=none).
  • The same pelican prompt was run on GPT‑5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna for side‑by‑side comparison.

⚙️ Model variants and reasoning levels

  • GPT‑6 Astra – reasoning levels: low, medium, high, xhigh, max.
  • GPT‑5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna – same prompt, default reasoning levels.

📊 Key observations

  • Astra pelicans are described as “much better.”
  • The very best GPT‑5.6‑Sol pelican (xhigh) is still “pretty clearly a bunch of abstract shapes.”
  • Every Astra pelican from low to xhigh looks better than any GPT‑5.6‑Sol result.
  • The Astra max‑level pelican is “really good,” though it sometimes fails to place legs on both sides of the frame.
  • Astra low produces a better pelican than any GPT‑5.6‑Sol model at any level, for 9.55 cents.
  • Spending 10 cents on any other model gets a much worse result.

💰 Cost and token usage

Model Input tokens Input price (per million) Output price (per million)
Astra 16 $10 $50
Luna 16
Sol 26 $5 $30
Terra 26
  • Astra’s price is roughly twice that of Sol, but it uses significantly fewer tokens, making the effective cost difference smaller.

🤔 Open questions

  • The identical input token count for Astra and Luna leads to the comment: “I wonder if Astra and Luna are more related to each other than OpenAI let on?”

See the grid for full quality images.
